analysis:
This is a docs-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md; no executable code or config changed. I examined both head-text units (lines 1211-2032), the changed ranges and the patch excerpt. The excerpt is truncated, so the last hunk is only partially visible.

Changed content:
1. GLM5Next video: variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime is now indexed rather than refused. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate. This is documented around lines 810-829 (patch only, outside the supplied head units). It widens the accepted video input surface in the provider media decoder (TB-007, T-050 area), but the decoded-frame cap of 512 MiB and the prepared-pixel cap of 28,532 visual tokens are still stated. The documented behavior is that processor refusals remain deterministic 400s and tower/MLX faults keep the retriable refusal. I cannot verify the code behind this, so the unverified contract is the new VFR path's memory and frame bounds.
2. Inline video labels (lines 1896-1899): data:video/mp4, x-m4v, quicktime and mov are admitted by base64 header. Container identity is enforced from the bytes by MemoryBackedVideoAsset, so the label only gates the part. This does not weaken the earlier T-050 mitigation, which concerns not writing plaintext video to temp files. The doc says the asset is memory-backed, which is consistent with it.

Other content in the units is pre-existing context: the Vision constraints and media caps (lines 1886-1895), the prefix-cache and SSD statements consistent with T-041, deadline and MTP descriptions, and sampling and tool-parser tables. I saw no statement that loosens prefix-cache TTL, scoping or HMAC naming, so SEC-035 is unaffected. There is no evidence of a regression in authorization, attestation, encryption or billing.

Integration questions: confirm that the underlying GLM5NextProcessor VFR indexing code enforces the frame-count, duration (600 s) and decoded-byte caps for tracks with unusual or zero nominalFrameRate, and that no temp-file path was introduced.
